Let me think through this logically based on standard clinical trial design principles:

In a placebo-controlled trial where we're testing a new treatment (antisense oligonucleotide) in addition to standard therapy (dacarbazine), the typical design would be:

1. Group A (verum/experimental group): Receives the standard therapy PLUS the new treatment
2. Group B (control group): Receives the standard therapy PLUS a placebo (instead of the new treatment)

This design allows researchers to isolate the effect of the new treatment while ensuring all patients receive the standard of care therapy.

In this case:
- Standard therapy = dacarbazine
- New treatment = antisense oligonucleotide against bcl-2
- Group A (verum) = antisense oligonucleotides + dacarbazine
- Group B (control) = dacarbazine + placebo

Looking at the options, this matches option E: A = antisense oligonucleotides + dacarbazine and B = dacarbazine + placebo

This is the ethically appropriate design because it ensures all patients receive the standard treatment (dacarbazine) while testing whether adding the antisense oligonucleotide provides additional benefit.

Final Answer: [ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
